event: Aircraft 469 (MARSOC) aborted its VTOL launch at about 100 ft AGL with a VTOL controller GPS fault, and did the same on a second launch on 8/7.
component: GPS signal quality (C/N0 below 40 abort threshold)
failure_mode: GPS C/N0 dropped into the 30s during VTOL climbout, triggering the designed climb abort
contributing: customer-added HackRF One, Raspberry Pi and GPS antenna puck with magnetic mount on tailboom (likely RF interference)

evidence.quote: Operator received “Climb abort, VTOL controller fault Sensor: GPS Fault” On VTOL Control panel.
I took a quick look at both logs and noted that during VTOL climbout the CNo dropped deep into the 30’s in both instances.
@Pat Wells The aircraft will abort when the average of the top three CN0 values drop below 40. It is behaving as designed.
Note:  Operator stated that they have a Raspberry pie, HackRF One, and a GPS antenna puck with magnetic mount attached to tailboom.

team_root_cause: Degradation of GPS below threshold caused launch abort, per design. Likely cause is the listed extra equipment, some known to cause GPS interference.

would_settle_it.what: GCS VTOL Control window fault message from the 8/7 abort
GPS C/N0 with and without the HackRF, Raspberry Pi and extra antenna powered

reasoning: Both AARs show GPS C/N0 falling into the 30s during VTOL climbout, below the designed abort threshold of 40, so the abort worked as designed on a degraded GPS input. The customer had added a HackRF One and other RF equipment, which the team names as the likely interference source, but no interference check was done to prove it.
notes: Designed abort scored on the degraded input (GPS). Two events: 8/6 and 8/7 aborts. Interference source is inferred, not tested.

event: Aircraft 674 (Edge FLOPS, v6.2.10, E140 payload) showed an erratic icon heading on approach and ignored abort and GoTo commands, then completed a normal VTOL landing.
failure_mode: erroneous fixed-wing autopilot heading; GoTo command ignored because landing state machine was already in LAND_HOLD (by design)
contributing: possible magnetic interference from Octopus E140Z G2 payload or gimbal position differing from mag cal
operator continued recovery despite icon anomaly
hand controller abort not found in any log

evidence.quote: @David Grosher @Greg Fryer @Pat Wells on a quick data review it looks to me like the heading from the fixed-wing ap was erroneous for some reason.
Previously have noted magnetometer issues on other Edge asset VXE30’s during preflight with E140 payload installed.
@Pat Wells I can’t say definitively if the issues were related to E140 or something else, although it seems likely if we’ve had issues with that payload.
- I don’t see any evidence in any of the logs (GCS Debug/GCS Event/XComm Event) of this abort.
So the fixed wing ignored the go to command and completed the VTOL landing.

team_root_cause: Not an issue. No evidence of abort in logs. Goto was ignored because it was too far along in the landing sequence.
disagreement: The team closed it as not an issue because the ignored GoTo was by design, which I accept for the command handling. But the trigger of the event, the erratic icon and altitude, was a real fault: “it looks to me like the heading from the fixed-wing ap was erroneous for some reason.” That heading error, likely magnetometer related, was never resolved on this ticket.

would_settle_it.what: FWAP vs VTOL AP heading and magnetometer channels through the approach

would_settle_it.file: GCS mag check with E140 in flight position
would_settle_it.what: FWAP heading error with E140 gimbal in flight position versus stowed

reasoning: Engineers found the fixed-wing autopilot heading erroneous, which explains the crabbing icon and erratic approach. The aircraft carried an E140 payload, which had caused magnetometer problems on other aircraft, but no mag check was done, and replacing the FWAP was the other option offered. The ignored GoTo was correct behavior for the LAND_HOLD state, and the hand controller abort never reached the logs.
notes: Two issues on one ticket: heading error and ignored commands. Command handling judged by design per FS2-2196. Why the hand controller abort left no log entry was not explained.

The root cause of increased resistance and subsequent overheating is the connector sits too high above the plug and does not fully engage.
A diameter, measured with a pin gage, of .273 or less will cause the problem.

team_view_in_comments: Problem has been isolated down to the AS150 connector on the Main battery.

event: Systemic investigation, started from the aircraft 692 main battery overheat, into recent AS150 battery connectors (main batteries and HLBs) that are hard to mate and demate and can sit partly engaged, causing heating.
component: AS150 power contact socket (PN 100-100804) in battery mating cable
failure_mode: socket inner diameter undersized (0.273 in or less) against 0.275 in pin, press fit instead of slip fit, plug does not fully engage, high resistance and heating
contributing: COTS hobby-grade contacts with no controlled dimensions
Amass pins about .038 in shorter than nominal (NCR)

evidence.quote: - further investigate root cause - what in the connector failed? The AS150 pins do not fit the AS150 receptacles. The inner diameter of the receptacle is too small for the outer diameter of the pin. It is more of a press fit than a slip fit.

@Cameron Chapman @Sloan Payne Data is posted. I measured a few different batteries and found that an inner diameter on the receptacle of .273 or less will cause a defect. Has to be measured with a pin gage.
The root cause of increased resistance and subsequent overheating is the connector sits too high above the plug and does not fully engage.
A diameter, measured with a pin gage, of .273 or less will cause the problem.
- Brad then measured receptacle size using pin gauges and compared that to removal force for each battery. Correlation was seen between undersized pins and strong pull force needed

team_view_in_comments: The inner diameter of the receptacle is too small for the outer diameter of the pin.
reasoning: Pin gage measurements show recent sockets at 0.271 to 0.274 in against 0.275 in pins, and pull force rises as socket diameter falls, with 0.273 in or less judged defective. A load test showed 3 of 5 batteries lost 6 V at 1 A with a 0.05 in mating gap, which explains the heating in VXEP-539. Containment sorted sockets at 0.275 in and pull testing then showed no excess force.
notes: No Root Cause field. Pin side tracked in VXEP-326 and pin depth in ENG-2655 (not read). proposedChange 114-106509.xlsx converted as an empty sheet. Other linked incidents (VXEP-761, 834, 985, 999, VA-1903) not read as they are separate events.
